meta.title: Elasticsearch Compliance: Audit Trails, Access Tracking & Immutable Indices | Search Guard
meta.description: Meet GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX and ISO 27001 requirements for Elasticsearch: read and write history, immutable indices, field anonymization, encryption and audit logging with Search Guard.
title.headline: Compliance for Elasticsearch
title.text: Regulations like GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX and ISO 27001 all come down to the same questions: who can see sensitive data, who accessed it, what changed — and can you prove it? Search Guard answers them inside your Elasticsearch cluster, with audit trails your auditors can rely on.
title.buttonAudit: Talk to us about your audit
auditor.headline: Answer the questions your auditor will ask
auditor.intro: Compliance isn't a checkbox — it's evidence. These are the questions that come up in every audit, and how Search Guard answers them.
auditor.q1.question: "Who can see personal data?"
auditor.q1.answer: Role-based access control down to individual documents and fields decides who sees what. Field anonymization goes further: selected roles see sensitive values as hashes or masked strings instead of clear text — while aggregations and analytics keep working.
auditor.q1.features: Document- and field-level security · Field anonymization
auditor.q2.question: "Who read this data, and when?"
auditor.q2.answer: Read history records every access to the indices and fields you mark as sensitive: when, by which user, which document, and which watched fields were part of the result. Fields hidden by field-level security don't trigger an event — the trail shows real exposure, not noise.
auditor.q3.question: "What changed, and who changed it?"
auditor.q3.answer: Write history tracks document creation, deletion and field-level changes as exact diffs — including deletions of personal data, so you can document that erasure requests were carried out. Configuration change tracking and system change tracking cover changes to Search Guard and Elasticsearch settings themselves.
auditor.q3.features: Write history · Configuration change tracking · System change tracking
auditor.q4.question: "Can the evidence be trusted?"
auditor.q4.answer: Immutable indices follow the write-once, read-many principle: documents can be added, but never changed or deleted — and the index itself can't be deleted, closed or reindexed. Store your audit trail there, or route audit events to external storage and SIEM systems, category by category.
auditor.q4.features: Immutable indices · Audit event routing to multiple endpoints
auditor.q5.question: "Is the data protected in transit and at rest?"
auditor.q5.answer: Search Guard enforces TLS for all REST and node-to-node traffic. Search Guard Encryption at Rest encrypts your indices at the Lucene level, with keys kept in memory and never written to disk.
auditor.q6.question: "Would you notice a breach in progress?"
auditor.q6.answer: Audit events are data — so Signals, Search Guard's alerting engine, can watch them. Get notified about a spike in failed logins, privilege errors, or unexpected access to watched fields, via email, Slack, PagerDuty, Jira or webhooks.
architecture.headline: From event to evidence
architecture.text: Search Guard generates audit events inside every node — login failures, missing privileges, reads of sensitive fields, document changes, configuration changes. You decide where they go: an audit index on the same cluster, an immutable index, a separate Elasticsearch cluster, a webhook, or any log4j appender such as Kafka or syslog. Route security events to your SIEM and compliance events to long-term storage — at the same time.
anonViews.headline: Same data, different views
anonViews.text: An analyst and a compliance officer run the same query on the same index. The analyst sees hashed email addresses and masked names; the compliance officer sees clear text. No copies, no ETL — anonymization happens on the fly, per role.
gallery.headline: Audit evidence you can show

faq.headline: Compliance questions
faq.q1.question: Does Search Guard make us GDPR compliant?
faq.q1.answer: No software can do that on its own — compliance also depends on your processes and organization. Search Guard provides the technical controls your Elasticsearch stack needs: access restriction, pseudonymization, encryption, and verifiable audit trails.
faq.q2.question: Where are audit logs stored?
faq.q2.answer: Wherever you choose: an index on the same cluster, an immutable index, a separate Elasticsearch cluster, a webhook, or any log4j appender. The Compliance Edition can route different event categories to different destinations at the same time.
faq.q3.question: Can audit logs be tampered with?
faq.q3.answer: Store them in an immutable index and documents can't be changed or deleted afterwards. For separation of duties, ship them to an external cluster or SIEM that administrators of the monitored cluster can't access.
faq.q4.question: What's the performance impact?
faq.q4.answer: Read and write history only watch the indices and fields you configure, so overhead stays where you need the evidence. You can also log metadata only, excluding document content.
